transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have $6,000,000 outstanding under the central-bank liquidity facility, currently secured by $10,000,000 in government bonds. We're looking to substitute part of that collateral with investment-grade corporate bonds so we can free up some government bonds for an upcoming client settlement. The facility requires collateral valued at least 1.25 times the outstanding borrowing, so we need to make sure any substitution keeps us comfortably above that threshold. Before I sign off on this, I need each of you to report any relevant requirements or concerns from your areas: collateral risk, legal, treasury operations, and relationship coverage. What do we need to consider here?

transcript.text: To help Mara assess the substitution, let me walk through the collateral math. The corporate bond basket I identified has a market value of $9,400,000 with a 20% haircut, which gives a collateral value of $7,520,000. The facility requires collateral valued at least 1.25 times the $6,000,000 outstanding, so we need a minimum collateral value of $7,500,000. That means the corporate bond basket alone would just barely clear the threshold by $20,000 — but that's before we account for Leila's requirement to release $9,000,000 of government bonds for the client settlement. If we release $9,000,000 of the current $10,000,000 in government bonds, only $1,000,000 in government bonds would remain. Assuming government bonds carry no haircut, that $1,000,000 plus the $7,520,000 from the corporate basket gives $8,520,000 in total collateral value against the $7,500,000 requirement — a surplus of about $1,020,000. So from a pure collateral-coverage standpoint, the substitution looks viable, though the margin is something Mara should consider. I'd also note that Nadia's 30% single-issuer limit needs to be checked against the basket composition before we finalize, and I still need to upload the basket analysis to the facility file.
